title: Osteoporosis: fracture risk and drug treatment
subject: endocrinology
setting: Outpatient, primary care, fracture liaison, endocrinology
summary: Assess fracture risk with FRAX and DXA (osteoporosis: T-score -2.5 or lower, or a hip or vertebral fragility fracture), treat high risk with alendronate 70 mg weekly or zoledronic acid 5 mg IV yearly, consider an anabolic drug first at very high risk, never stop denosumab without follow-on therapy, and ensure calcium and vitamin D.

sections.title: Who to assess and how to diagnose
items: Assess postmenopausal women and men aged 50 or over with a clinical risk factor: prior fragility fracture, oral glucocorticoids, parental hip fracture, low BMI, smoking, high alcohol intake, rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, falls, early menopause, hypogonadism or androgen deprivation.
Fragility fracture: a fracture from a fall from standing height or less. Vertebral fractures are often silent: look for height loss of 4 cm or more, kyphosis or acute back pain.
Use FRAX (10-year probability of major osteoporotic and hip fracture), with or without femoral neck BMD, using the model for the patient's country of birth, to decide on DXA and treatment.
Osteoporosis: DXA T-score -2.5 or lower at lumbar spine, femoral neck, total hip or one-third radius. A low-trauma hip or vertebral fracture establishes osteoporosis regardless of BMD (AACE).

Vertebral fracture assessment (lateral spine X-ray or DXA VFA) if height loss of 4 cm or more, kyphosis, current or recent long-term oral glucocorticoids, T-score -2.5 or lower, or acute back pain with risk factors (NOGG).

sections.title: Investigations for secondary causes
items: Routine: full blood count, ESR or CRP, calcium, albumin, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, creatinine and eGFR, liver enzymes, thyroid function and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (NOGG).

If indicated: serum protein electrophoresis, immunoglobulins and free light chains (myeloma), PTH if calcium is raised, coeliac serology, testosterone, SHBG, LH and FSH in men, prolactin, tests for Cushing syndrome, urinary calcium.
Persistently low phosphate or alkaline phosphatase suggests another metabolic bone disease such as osteomalacia: investigate before starting an antiresorptive.
Premenopausal women and men under 50 with fragility fractures: use Z-scores and refer for specialist investigation.
Dental review before bisphosphonates or denosumab when dental disease is present, without delaying treatment after a fracture.

sections.title: Who to treat
items: Treat after a hip or vertebral fragility fracture (even with osteopenia), with a T-score of -2.5 or lower, or with osteopenia and a high FRAX probability (AACE, US thresholds: major osteoporotic fracture 20% or more, or hip 3% or more; NOGG uses age-dependent UK thresholds).

Very high risk: recent fracture (within 12 to 24 months), fracture on treatment, 2 or more vertebral fractures, very low T-score (below -3.0 AACE; -3.5 or lower NOGG), high-dose glucocorticoids, injurious falls, or FRAX well above threshold (AACE: major fracture above 30%, hip above 4.5%). Refer to a specialist.

Glucocorticoids: start bone protection with the steroid, without waiting for DXA, in anyone with a prior fragility fracture, women aged 70 or over, and postmenopausal women or men 50 or over taking prednisolone 7.5 mg/day or more for 3 months or longer (NOGG).

Everyone: calcium intake at least 700 mg/day (NOGG; AACE 1200 mg/day for women 50 or over), preferably from diet; vitamin D at least 800 IU/day if deficient or at risk; weight-bearing and strengthening exercise; stop smoking; alcohol 2 units/day or less; falls assessment.

sections.title: Drug choice
items: High risk: oral alendronate 70 mg once weekly or risedronate 35 mg once weekly, or IV zoledronic acid 5 mg once yearly (first line after hip fracture and when oral drugs are not tolerated or absorbed).
Denosumab 60 mg SC every 6 months is an alternative first-line drug; it must not be delayed or stopped without follow-on therapy because of rebound vertebral fractures.

Very high risk, especially with vertebral fractures: consider an anabolic drug first (teriparatide 20 mcg SC daily for up to 24 months, abaloparatide 80 mcg SC daily for 18 months, or romosozumab 210 mg SC monthly for 12 months), then start an antiresorptive without delay.
Romosozumab: do not use after myocardial infarction or stroke or at high cardiovascular risk.
HRT is a first-line option for women aged 60 or under with high fracture risk and low risk of breast cancer and VTE (NOGG 2024). Raloxifene 60 mg daily reduces vertebral fractures only.
Men: alendronate, risedronate, zoledronic acid, denosumab or teriparatide; romosozumab and abaloparatide are licensed only for postmenopausal women (NOGG).

sections.title: Duration and monitoring
items: Oral bisphosphonate: reassess FRAX and BMD after 5 years. Continue to 10 years if aged 70 or over at start, prior hip or vertebral fracture, prednisolone 7.5 mg/day or more, or a fracture on treatment; otherwise consider a treatment break (NOGG).
Zoledronic acid: reassess after 3 years; continue to 6 years in the same higher-risk groups.
During a bisphosphonate break, reassess after 18 months (risedronate, ibandronate), 2 years (alendronate) or 3 years (zoledronic acid), or at once after a new fracture.
Denosumab has no drug holiday. If it must stop, give zoledronic acid 6 months after the last injection and use CTX to time further doses; if CTX is unavailable, repeat zoledronic acid 6 months later.

DXA every 1 to 3 years to judge response (lumbar spine preferred). Two or more fragility fractures on treatment suggest failure: check adherence (below 80% is poor) and secondary causes, and switch drug.
Ask patients to report thigh, groin or hip pain (atypical femoral fracture: image both femurs) and oral symptoms (osteonecrosis of the jaw); encourage routine dental care.

sections.title: Kidney function and drug safety
items: Zoledronic acid is contraindicated at GFR 35 mL/min or less and risedronate at 30 mL/min or less; alendronate (35 or less) and ibandronate (30 or less) are cautioned. Use creatinine clearance if over 75 or BMI below 18 or above 40 kg/m2.

Correct vitamin D deficiency and hypocalcaemia before zoledronic acid or denosumab (for example colecalciferol 100,000 to 300,000 IU orally in divided doses). Check calcium before each denosumab dose, and at 2 weeks after the first dose if creatinine clearance is below 35 mL/min.
Oral bisphosphonates: after an overnight fast with a glass (about 200 mL) of plain water, at least 30 minutes before food, drink, calcium or other medicines, staying upright for 30 minutes.
Zoledronic acid often causes a flu-like acute phase reaction after the first infusion; paracetamol reduces it.
Teriparatide is contraindicated with hypercalcaemia, severe renal impairment, skeletal malignancy or prior skeletal radiation; check PTH is normal before starting.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Stopping denosumab or letting a dose run more than 6 months late: rapid bone loss and multiple vertebral fractures.
Missing a hip or vertebral fracture as the trigger for treatment; fracture liaison services close this gap.
Starting a bisphosphonate in unrecognised osteomalacia or hypocalcaemia.
Routine drug holidays for everyone: stopping treatment increases fracture risk, so base breaks on reassessed risk.

Routine intermittent large vitamin D doses (60,000 IU or more), common in India, may increase falls and fractures (NOGG); reserve high doses for documented deficiency and prefer daily dosing for maintenance.

drugs.name: Alendronic acid
drugs.notes: Fasting, upright for 30 minutes. Caution at GFR 35 mL/min or less. Reassess at 5 years.

drugs.name: Risedronate
drugs.notes: Contraindicated at GFR 30 mL/min or less.

drugs.name: Zoledronic acid
drugs.dose: 5 mg IV infusion over at least 15 minutes once yearly
drugs.notes: Contraindicated at GFR 35 mL/min or less. Replete vitamin D and calcium first. First line after hip fracture. Reassess at 3 years.

drugs.name: Denosumab
drugs.notes: Never stop without follow-on zoledronic acid 6 months after the last dose. Check calcium before each dose; hypocalcaemia risk rises in CKD.

drugs.name: Teriparatide
drugs.dose: 20 mcg SC once daily for up to 24 months
drugs.notes: Very high risk. Follow with alendronate, zoledronic acid or denosumab.

drugs.name: Abaloparatide
drugs.dose: 80 mcg SC once daily for up to 18 months
drugs.notes: Postmenopausal women at high or very high risk. Follow with an antiresorptive.

drugs.name: Romosozumab
drugs.dose: 210 mg SC once monthly (two 105 mg injections) for 12 months
drugs.notes: Postmenopausal women at very high risk. Not after myocardial infarction or stroke. Follow with an antiresorptive.

drugs.name: Raloxifene
drugs.notes: Reduces vertebral fractures only. Contraindicated with prior VTE.

drugs.name: Calcium and colecalciferol
drugs.dose: Total calcium intake 700 to 1200 mg/day (diet first, supplement if low); colecalciferol 800 to 2000 IU/day
drugs.notes: Adjunct to all anti-osteoporosis drugs when intake or vitamin D status is low.
